items.readable_text:
Content:
We've seen how to calculate the total derivative of a function [MATH: f: \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R.] In this lesson, we will learn how to calculate its second derivative.

Content:
For a function [MATH: f: \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R,] given by

Content:
[MATH: [x_{1}; x_{2}; ⋮; x_{n}]]

Content:
the total derivative of [MATH: f] is given by the matrix

Content:
[MATH: [(∂f)/(∂x_{1})|(∂f)/(∂x_{2})|⋯|(∂f)/(∂x_{n})]]

Content:
To differentiate [MATH: f] once more, we first need to take the transpose of the first derivative:

Content:
[MATH: [(∂f)/(∂x_{1}); (∂f)/(∂x_{2}); ⋮; (∂f)/(∂x_{n})]]

Content:
To calculate the second derivative of [MATH: f,] we simply apply the definition of the total derivative to [MATH: \left(\boldsymbol f'(\mathbf x)\right)^T.] By doing this, we get the following [MATH: n\times n] matrix:

Content:
[MATH: [(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{1}^{2})|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{1}∂x_{2})|⋯|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{1}∂x_{n}); (∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{2}∂x_{1})|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{2}^{2})|⋯|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{2}∂x_{n}); ⋮|⋮|⋮|⋮; (∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{n}∂x_{1})|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{n}∂x_{2})|⋯|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{n}^{2})]]

Content:
Notice that this matrix is symmetric due to the equality of mixed partial derivatives. This becomes important later.

Content:
The matrix [MATH: \boldsymbol{f}''(\mathbf x)] is sometimes called the Hessian matrix, and its determinant,

Content:
[MATH: H(\mathbf x) = \det\big( \boldsymbol{f}''(\mathbf x) \big)]

Content:
is called the Hessian determinant.

Content:
Note that in the case of a two-variable function [MATH: f(x,y),] the second derivative is given by

Content:
[MATH: [(∂^{2}f)/(∂x^{2})|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x∂y); (∂^{2}f)/(∂y∂x)|(∂^{2}f)/(∂y^{2})]]

Content:
In this lesson, we'll primarily focus on two-variable functions [MATH: f(x,y).] However, we should remember that the techniques discussed here can be applied to scalar functions with an arbitrary number of variables.

sections.normalized_html: Find [MATH: \boldsymbol f''(\pi,0)] for the function [MATH: f(x,y)] given that [MATH: [e^{y}\cos x|e^{y}\sin x]]
sections.readable_text:
Find [MATH: \boldsymbol f''(\pi,0)] for the function [MATH: f(x,y)] given that
[MATH: [e^{y}\cos x|e^{y}\sin x]]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
For a function [MATH: f: \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R,] given by [MATH: [x_{1}; x_{2}; ⋮; x_{n}]]

the second derivative of [MATH: f] is given by the [MATH: n\times n] matrix

[MATH: [(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{1}^{2})|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{1}∂x_{2})|⋯|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{1}∂x_{n}); (∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{2}∂x_{1})|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{2}^{2})|⋯|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{2}∂x_{n}); ⋮|⋮|⋮|⋮; (∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{n}∂x_{1})|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{n}∂x_{2})|⋯|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{n}^{2})]]

In our case, we have

[MATH: [(∂^{2}f)/(∂x^{2})|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x∂y); (∂^{2}f)/(∂y∂x)|(∂^{2}f)/(∂y^{2})]]

First, notice that since [MATH: [e^{y}\cos x|e^{y}\sin x]] we must have

[MATH: \dfrac{\partial f}{\partial x} = e^y\cos x , \qquad \dfrac{\partial f}{\partial y} =e^y\sin x .]

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

[MATH: (∂^{2}f)/(∂x^{2})|= (∂)/(∂x)(e^{y}\cos x) = − e^{y}\sin x|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x∂y)|= (∂)/(∂x)(e^{y}\sin x) = e^{y}\cos x; (∂^{2}f)/(∂y∂x)|= (∂)/(∂y)(e^{y}\cos x) = e^{y}\cos x|(∂^{2}f)/(∂y^{2})|= (∂)/(∂y)(e^{y}\sin x) = e^{y}\sin x]

So, the second derivative is

[MATH: f^{″}(x, y)|= [− e^{y}\sin x|e^{y}\cos x; e^{y}\cos x|e^{y}\sin x].]

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at [MATH: (\pi,0).] This gives

[MATH: [0|− 1; − 1|0]]

sections.normalized_html: Find [MATH: \boldsymbol f''(1,0)] for the function [MATH: f(x,y) = x^2 e^y.]
sections.readable_text: Find [MATH: \boldsymbol f''(1,0)] for the function [MATH: f(x,y) = x^2 e^y.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
For a function [MATH: f: \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R,] given by [MATH: [x_{1}; x_{2}; ⋮; x_{n}]]

the second derivative of [MATH: f] is given by the [MATH: n\times n] matrix

[MATH: [(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{1}^{2})|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{1}∂x_{2})|⋯|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{1}∂x_{n}); (∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{2}∂x_{1})|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{2}^{2})|⋯|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{2}∂x_{n}); ⋮|⋮|⋮|⋮; (∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{n}∂x_{1})|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{n}∂x_{2})|⋯|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{n}^{2})]]

In our case, we have

[MATH: [(∂^{2}f)/(∂x^{2})|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x∂y); (∂^{2}f)/(∂y∂x)|(∂^{2}f)/(∂y^{2})]]

First, we compute the first derivative of [MATH: f(x,y),] as follows:

[MATH: f^{′}(x, y)|= [(∂f)/(∂x)|(∂f)/(∂y)]; = [(∂)/(∂x)(x^{2}e^{y})|(∂)/(∂y)(x^{2}e^{y})]; = [2xe^{y}|x^{2}e^{y}]]

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

[MATH: (∂^{2}f)/(∂x^{2})|= (∂)/(∂x)(2xe^{y}) = 2e^{y}|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x∂y)|= (∂)/(∂x)(x^{2}e^{y}) = 2xe^{y}; (∂^{2}f)/(∂y∂x)|= (∂)/(∂y)(2xe^{y}) = 2xe^{y}|(∂^{2}f)/(∂y^{2})|= (∂)/(∂y)(x^{2}e^{y}) = x^{2}e^{y}]

So, the second derivative is

[MATH: f^{″}(x, y)|= [2e^{y}|2xe^{y}; 2xe^{y}|x^{2}e^{y}].]

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at [MATH: \left(1,0\right).] This gives

[MATH: f^{″}(1, 0) = [2|2; 2|1].]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
We've seen how to calculate the total derivative of a function [MATH: f: \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R.] In this lesson, we will learn how to calculate its second derivative.

Content:
For a function [MATH: f: \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R,] given by

Content:
[MATH: [x_{1}; x_{2}; ⋮; x_{n}]]

Content:
the total derivative of [MATH: f] is given by the matrix

Content:
[MATH: [(∂f)/(∂x_{1})|(∂f)/(∂x_{2})|⋯|(∂f)/(∂x_{n})]]

Content:
To differentiate [MATH: f] once more, we first need to take the transpose of the first derivative:

Content:
[MATH: [(∂f)/(∂x_{1}); (∂f)/(∂x_{2}); ⋮; (∂f)/(∂x_{n})]]

Content:
To calculate the second derivative of [MATH: f,] we simply apply the definition of the total derivative to [MATH: \left(\boldsymbol f'(\mathbf x)\right)^T.] By doing this, we get the following [MATH: n\times n] matrix:

Content:
[MATH: [(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{1}^{2})|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{1}∂x_{2})|⋯|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{1}∂x_{n}); (∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{2}∂x_{1})|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{2}^{2})|⋯|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{2}∂x_{n}); ⋮|⋮|⋮|⋮; (∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{n}∂x_{1})|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{n}∂x_{2})|⋯|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{n}^{2})]]

Content:
Notice that this matrix is symmetric due to the equality of mixed partial derivatives. This becomes important later.

Content:
The matrix [MATH: \boldsymbol{f}''(\mathbf x)] is sometimes called the Hessian matrix, and its determinant,

Content:
[MATH: H(\mathbf x) = \det\big( \boldsymbol{f}''(\mathbf x) \big)]

Content:
is called the Hessian determinant.

Content:
Note that in the case of a two-variable function [MATH: f(x,y),] the second derivative is given by

Content:
[MATH: [(∂^{2}f)/(∂x^{2})|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x∂y); (∂^{2}f)/(∂y∂x)|(∂^{2}f)/(∂y^{2})]]

Content:
In this lesson, we'll primarily focus on two-variable functions [MATH: f(x,y).] However, we should remember that the techniques discussed here can be applied to scalar functions with an arbitrary number of variables.

---

Item 2 — Example: Finding the Second Derivative of a Function Given Its First Derivative

Example Prompt:
Find [MATH: \boldsymbol f''(\pi,0)] for the function [MATH: f(x,y)] given that
[MATH: [e^{y}\cos x|e^{y}\sin x]]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
For a function [MATH: f: \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R,] given by
[MATH: [x_{1}; x_{2}; ⋮; x_{n}]]

the second derivative of [MATH: f] is given by the [MATH: n\times n] matrix

[MATH: [(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{1}^{2})|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{1}∂x_{2})|⋯|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{1}∂x_{n}); (∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{2}∂x_{1})|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{2}^{2})|⋯|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{2}∂x_{n}); ⋮|⋮|⋮|⋮; (∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{n}∂x_{1})|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{n}∂x_{2})|⋯|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{n}^{2})]]

In our case, we have

[MATH: [(∂^{2}f)/(∂x^{2})|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x∂y); (∂^{2}f)/(∂y∂x)|(∂^{2}f)/(∂y^{2})]]

First, notice that since [MATH: [e^{y}\cos x|e^{y}\sin x]]
we must have

[MATH: \dfrac{\partial f}{\partial x} = e^y\cos x ,
\qquad
\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial y} =e^y\sin x .]

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

[MATH: (∂^{2}f)/(∂x^{2})|= (∂)/(∂x)(e^{y}\cos x) = − e^{y}\sin x|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x∂y)|= (∂)/(∂x)(e^{y}\sin x) = e^{y}\cos x; (∂^{2}f)/(∂y∂x)|= (∂)/(∂y)(e^{y}\cos x) = e^{y}\cos x|(∂^{2}f)/(∂y^{2})|= (∂)/(∂y)(e^{y}\sin x) = e^{y}\sin x]

So, the second derivative is

[MATH: f^{″}(x, y)|= [− e^{y}\sin x|e^{y}\cos x; e^{y}\cos x|e^{y}\sin x].]

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at [MATH: (\pi,0).] This gives

[MATH: [0|− 1; − 1|0]]

Item 5 — Example: Finding the Second Derivative of a Function

Example Prompt:
Find [MATH: \boldsymbol f''(1,0)] for the function [MATH: f(x,y) = x^2 e^y.]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
For a function [MATH: f: \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R,] given by
[MATH: [x_{1}; x_{2}; ⋮; x_{n}]]

the second derivative of [MATH: f] is given by the [MATH: n\times n] matrix

[MATH: [(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{1}^{2})|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{1}∂x_{2})|⋯|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{1}∂x_{n}); (∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{2}∂x_{1})|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{2}^{2})|⋯|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{2}∂x_{n}); ⋮|⋮|⋮|⋮; (∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{n}∂x_{1})|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{n}∂x_{2})|⋯|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x_{n}^{2})]]

In our case, we have

[MATH: [(∂^{2}f)/(∂x^{2})|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x∂y); (∂^{2}f)/(∂y∂x)|(∂^{2}f)/(∂y^{2})]]

First, we compute the first derivative of [MATH: f(x,y),] as follows:

[MATH: f^{′}(x, y)|= [(∂f)/(∂x)|(∂f)/(∂y)]; = [(∂)/(∂x)(x^{2}e^{y})|(∂)/(∂y)(x^{2}e^{y})]; = [2xe^{y}|x^{2}e^{y}]]

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

[MATH: (∂^{2}f)/(∂x^{2})|= (∂)/(∂x)(2xe^{y}) = 2e^{y}|(∂^{2}f)/(∂x∂y)|= (∂)/(∂x)(x^{2}e^{y}) = 2xe^{y}; (∂^{2}f)/(∂y∂x)|= (∂)/(∂y)(2xe^{y}) = 2xe^{y}|(∂^{2}f)/(∂y^{2})|= (∂)/(∂y)(x^{2}e^{y}) = x^{2}e^{y}]

So, the second derivative is

[MATH: f^{″}(x, y)|= [2e^{y}|2xe^{y}; 2xe^{y}|x^{2}e^{y}].]

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at [MATH: \left(1,0\right).] This gives

[MATH: f^{″}(1, 0) = [2|2; 2|1].]
